titles: Tarp and rope for roof damage

list_child.name: listRequests
list_child.desc: Retrieves the full list of aid requests currently logged in the relief system. Use this when you need to see everything survivors have asked for, regardless of status.

get_child.name: getRequest
get_child.desc: Retrieves a single aid request record using its unique id. This is the way to pull full detail on one request instead of scanning the whole list.

list_parent.name: listSurvivors
list_parent.desc: Retrieves the full roster of survivors who have filed one or more aid requests with the relief operation. Use this to look up who is registered before filing or referencing a request.

get_parent.name: getSurvivor
get_parent.desc: Retrieves a single survivor record using its unique id. This is useful when you already have an id and just need that person's details.

delete_child.name: purgeRequest
delete_child.desc: Permanently deletes an aid request record from the system, and this action cannot be undone once it completes. Only use this for duplicate or erroneous entries, never for requests that were simply denied.

set_enum.name: setRequestState
set_enum.desc: Changes an aid request's state to intake, in_review, dispatched, or closed, reflecting where it stands in the relief workflow. Use this whenever a request moves forward or gets closed out.

set_bool.name: flagMedicalPriority
set_bool.desc: Marks an aid request as medically urgent so responders can triage it ahead of routine requests. This should only be used when there is a genuine health or safety concern attached to the request.

set_ref.name: reassignSurvivor
set_ref.desc: Moves an aid request onto a different survivor's record, which is useful when a request was logged under the wrong name. This does not change anything else about the request itself.

send.name: textSurvivor
send.desc: Sends a text message to a survivor's phone number on file, letting them know about a status change or asking for more information. This is the primary way field coordinators keep survivors informed.
